newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Imran Khan fails to vote in Pakistan elections.
newsitem.headline: Imran Khan fails to vote in Pakistan elections.

text.p: Former cricket captain-turned politician Imran Khan on Monday failed to cast what would have been his first vote in a Pakistani election.
Imran, who founded his Tehrik-i-Insaaf (Justice Movement) last year, appeared in his home town of Mianwali where he is registered, but found nobody from his own party to vote for.
He declined to vote for candidates of either of the two heavyweight parties, Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League or Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party.
"It was a question of either voting for the Muslim League or the People's Party," Imran told reporters.
"Neither of the two parties I feel have done justice in the past and I do not expect wonders from them now," he added.
"Unfortunately the Tehrik-i-Insaaf could not field a candidate in my constituency so therefore I am abstaining."

Pakistanis were voting in national and provincial assembly elections called by President Farooq Leghari after he dismissed Bhutto's government three months ago on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Imran, who led Pakistan to triumph in the 1992 cricket World Cup, has said he did not vote in previous elections because he was always out of the country playing cricket at the time.
A political novice, Imran himself is contesting nine constituencies, as permitted under electoral law, in his bid for a seat in the 217-member National Assembly (lower house).
Imran portrays himself as a new force that can clean up a political system he says has been sullied by Sharif, Bhutto, Leghari and Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari.
But a haggard, exhausted-looking Imran seemed doubtful about the prospects of his party's 132 National Assembly candidates.
"The PML obviously looks favourite to win the elctions. But it remains to be seen," he said.

"I think Tehrik-i-Insaaf might surprise people. We are not given much of a chance by experts, but I think they might get a shock because of the kind of support we have seen, especially if the silent majority comes out to vote today."
During the campaign Imran has been dogged by accusations that he has accepted "Zionist money" from his Jewish father-in-law Sir James Goldsmith. He denies the charges.
He has also been embarrassed by allegations by British heiress Sita White that he is the father of her four-year-old daughter Tyrian. He has called the claim a plot by his opponents.
Imran married Goldsmith's daughter Jemima, who converted to Islam, in 1995. They had a son, Suleiman Isa, late last year.
